messages:
maria: Hey team — customer acme-inc reports weird results from /v1/rerank: returned scores are negative and not normalized. Example: response shows scores [-3.12, -0.44, 0.02]. They expected probability-like values summing to 1. Happens on hosted prod, request id rq_0a1b2c3d. Can we confirm if this is a bug or expected? cc @ash :thinking:

ash: Thanks for the heads-up. Quick q: which model and rerank version were they using? Also can you paste the minimal request/response (no PII) and the X-Request-ID?

maria: Model reported: reh-rerank-001, rerank_version: v1. Request id: rq_0a1b2c3d. Minimal repro below:

```json
POST /v1/rerank
{
  "model":"reh-rerank-001",
  "input":"Which is the fastest open-source LLM?",
  "candidates":[
    "EleutherAI GPT-J is fast",
    "Redwood inference provides low latency",
    "Distil models might be faster"
  ],
  "top_k":3
}
```

Response they got:

```json
{
 "scores":[-3.12,-0.44,0.02],
 "rank":[2,1,0]
}
```

maria: Customer expected positive probabilities or similarity in 0..1. They're confused by negatives.

ash: Got it. Quick notes: rerank endpoints often return raw model scores (logits / log-likelihoods or other unnormalized metrics). Negative numbers are expected for log-probs. The endpoint doesn't implicitly softmax the scores. For ranking only the order matters. cc @evan for confirmation.

evan: Confirming — rerank-v1 returns unnormalized scores. Semantics: depending on the model variant it can be raw logits (can be negative), or a similarity metric (range depends on model, e.g., cosine -1..1). If the customer needs probabilities, they should apply softmax client-side across the candidate set. Example: 

```python
import math
scores = [-3.12, -0.44, 0.02]
exps = [math.exp(s) for s in scores]
probs = [e/sum(exps) for e in exps]
# probs -> approx [0.05, 0.36, 0.59]
```

evan: Also check model metadata in our model catalog: some rerank models expose "score_type" = "logit" or "cosine". If you see values outside expected numeric ranges (NaN, inf, >> absolute 1000) escalate — that could indicate a runtime bug or bad quantization.

leo: small add — input truncation affects score magnitude: longer candidates may get truncated which alters logit scale. Also note that pagination affects normalization: softmax should be computed across the exact candidate set you want probabilities over.

maria: Customer asked whether we can return server-side normalized probabilities (they want a param like score_type=probability). Is that supported out-of-the-box?

evan: Not currently. No server-side normalization option in v1. Feature request is reasonable; I will log it to the rerank roadmap. For now recommend client-side softmax or ask them to use our ranking helper that returns normalized scores (internal utility).

ash: For troubleshooting: ask customer to provide full request JSON (model, candidates, any headers), the X-Request-ID, timestamps, and whether they see identical scores across many requests (flat distribution). If scores are identical or NaN, escalate to eng-runtime with the request_id and a memory/worker trace.

maria: Drafted reply to customer: "Thanks — the rerank endpoint returns unnormalized model scores (logits or similarity metrics). Negative values are expected. Use softmax on the returned scores to obtain probabilities; otherwise use the ordering for ranking. See attached example. If you see NaN/inf or identical scores across different candidates please share the request id and we'll escalate." Sending now. :thumbsup:

rerank-bot: Note: deployment rerank-v1 last updated 2026-02-15. No active incidents. :white_check_mark:

ash: Follow-up question from customer: they page results and want consistent probabilities across pages. We should call that out: softmax across a single page won't be globally normalized. For global normalization you need to score all candidates in one request or use a fixed calibration set.

evan: Agreed — I'll add a short note to the docs and file a backlog ticket for an optional server-side "normalize=true" param. If they push for SLA change or claim regressions after a deploy, we'll escalate immediately.

leo: I'll put together a KB for CS with a short explanation, code snippets (softmax and detecting bad values), and typical causes (model type, truncation, quantization).

maria: Thanks everyone — closing unless the customer reopens. one more note: if a customer sees negative infinity or NaN in scores, escalate right away.
